# Executive summary {.unnumbered}

This report documents the Stage 1 (Process Design) evaluation of the A-Mab final
ultrafiltration / diafiltration (UF/DF) operation (Step 10), the tangential-flow-filtration
step that concentrates the virus-filtration pool and buffer-exchanges it into the final
formulation buffer to deliver the drug substance at its target concentration. In the A-Mab
case study this operation has **no drug-substance product-quality impact**: it is a
formulation / mass-balance operation, and the **formulation characterization** (excipient
levels, pH, osmolality and stability) is conducted and reported under the drug-product
development program rather than in this drug-substance characterization campaign. The
operation was therefore evaluated on a qualified bench-scale UF/DF model against its
process-performance measures, following the lifecycle approach to process validation
[@fda2011; @pdatr60; @ispegpg2023] and the Quality-by-Design principles of ICH Q8, Q9 and
Q11 [@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11], with the process model of the A-Mab case study [@amab2009].

`{python} n_params` process parameters were evaluated one factor at a time. The evaluation
confirms that UF/DF **forms or modifies no drug-substance product-quality CQA** and that it
robustly concentrates and buffer-exchanges the pool to the drug-substance target.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"""
**Key outcomes**

- No drug-substance product-quality CQA is set or modified by UF/DF; the glycan,
  charge-variant, aggregate and impurity attributes are established and cleared upstream and
  pass through the operation unchanged. Formulation attributes are characterized under the
  drug-product program and are out of scope here.
- The UF/DF step yield is **{pct(ufdf_yield)}** at the nominal condition
  ({mass_in:,} g product mass in, {mass_out:,} g out), completing the purification train at
  an overall process yield of **{pct(overall_yield)}** and delivering **{ds_mass_kg:.1f} kg**
  of drug substance.
- The operation delivers the drug substance at its target concentration of **{ds_conc:g} g/L**
  (final-concentration NOR {fc_nor_lo:g}–{fc_nor_hi:g} g/L), with diafiltration completing the
  exchange into the final formulation buffer.
- The number of diavolumes, the transmembrane pressure and the final DS concentration are all
  classified **KPP** (they govern buffer-exchange completeness, process flux/time and the
  final concentration — process performance — without a DS CQA impact). No parameter is a CPP.
""")
```

The UF/DF operation is demonstrated to be well understood and robust as a formulation /
mass-balance step. Because it forms no drug-substance product-quality attribute, its
parameter ranges and control are justified on process-performance grounds, and this report
rolls up into the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**).

# Introduction

## Product and unit operation

A-Mab is a humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody whose product-quality attributes — Fc
N-glycosylation, charge variants, aggregate and the process-related impurities — are
established in the production bioreactor and controlled (formed and cleared) through the
purification train [@amab2009]. Ultrafiltration / diafiltration is the final drug-substance
operation: a tangential-flow-filtration step in which ultrafiltration concentrates the
virus-filtration pool and diafiltration exchanges it into the final formulation buffer,
delivering the drug substance at its target concentration. The operation removes water and
exchanges buffer; it does not form, remove or modify any drug-substance product-quality
attribute, and is therefore evaluated here as a process-performance / mass-balance operation.
The formulation characterization proper — excipient levels, pH, osmolality and stability — is
conducted and reported under the drug-product development program.

## Objectives

The objectives of the evaluation were to (i) confirm that UF/DF has no impact on the
drug-substance product-quality CQAs; (ii) establish the effect of the operating parameters on
the process-performance measures — step yield, buffer-exchange completeness and the final DS
concentration; (iii) confirm that the drug substance is delivered at its target concentration
and buffer composition across the operating ranges; (iv) establish proven acceptable ranges
(PARs) and normal operating ranges (NORs) for each parameter; and (v) classify each parameter
and provide the ranges that justify the Stage 2 operating conditions and the control strategy.

## Regulatory and scientific basis

The work follows the lifecycle approach to process validation of the FDA 2011 guidance
[@fda2011], PDA Technical Report 60 [@pdatr60] and the ISPE Good Practice Guide
[@ispegpg2023], and applies the enhanced (QbD) development approach of ICH Q8, Q9 and Q11
[@ichq8; @ichq9; @ichq11]. Criticality is treated as a continuum (ICH Q9). The report
structure corresponds to the Stage 1 Process Design Report of PDA TR 60 §3.11 and provides
development-report content suitable to support a Biologics License Application; it is
correspondingly focused, because the operation forms no drug-substance CQA and the
formulation characterization is reported with the drug product.

# Prior knowledge and quality risk basis

## Platform and prior-product knowledge

The characterization ranges and set-points are supported by platform knowledge from related
humanized IgG1 antibodies and by A-Mab development and engineering experience [@amab2009].
Prior knowledge established that the glycan, charge-variant and aggregate CQAs are set in cell
culture and cleared through the purification train, and that a well-controlled UF/DF step
concentrates and buffer-exchanges the pool without altering these attributes: the antibody is
retained by the ultrafiltration membrane while water and small solutes permeate, so the
product-quality attributes are unchanged by the operation. This knowledge framed the
process-performance measures in scope and the decision to evaluate the operation univariately.

## Quality attributes and process-performance measures

UF/DF **sets or modifies no drug-substance product-quality CQA**; the CQAs established
upstream pass through the operation unchanged. The operation was therefore evaluated against
the process-performance measures it governs (@tbl-perf): the product (step) yield, the
buffer-exchange completeness delivered by the diafiltration, and the final DS concentration.
Formulation attributes (excipient concentrations, pH, osmolality) are drug-product
characterization endpoints and are addressed under the drug-product program, not here.

```{python}
#| output: asis
import pandas as pd
perf = pd.DataFrame([
    ["UF/DF step yield", f"{pct(ufdf_yield)}", "Mass balance across the final operation"],
    ["Final DS concentration", f"{ds_conc:g} g/L",
     f"Within NOR {fc_nor_lo:g}–{fc_nor_hi:g} g/L (@tbl-param)"],
    ["Buffer-exchange completeness", "Within target", "Diavolumes / residual old-buffer target"],
    ["Product-quality CQAs", "Unchanged", "Set and cleared upstream; not modified by UF/DF"],
], columns=["Process-performance measure", "Result at nominal condition", "Basis / criterion"])
show(perf)
```

: Process-performance measures evaluated for the UF/DF operation (no drug-substance product-quality CQA is set by this step). {#tbl-perf}

## Risk-based prioritization and parameter selection

Consistent with the A-Mab lifecycle of iterative risk assessments, the evaluation scope was
set by the Pre-Characterization Process Risk Assessment (**RA-001**). Because UF/DF carries no
credible risk of impact to a drug-substance product-quality CQA, none of its parameters was
assigned to a multivariate design of experiments; each parameter was evaluated one factor at a
time across its characterization range for its effect on the process-performance measures. The
parameters and ranges carried into this evaluation are given in @tbl-param.

# Materials and methods

## Scale-down model and its qualification

All runs were performed on a qualified bench-scale UF/DF (tangential-flow-filtration) model
representing the commercial operation — the platform membrane chemistry and molecular-weight
cut-off, operated at the commercial-equivalent membrane loading, transmembrane pressure and
cross-flow, with the same ultrafiltration-concentration and diafiltration-exchange sequence
(**SOP-2013**). The model was qualified against at-scale reference data (**SOP-1001**) by
comparing step yield, the final concentration and the buffer-exchange completeness, confirming
that the model is representative and suitable to support the parameter ranges [@pdatr60].

## Operation

The virus-filtration pool is concentrated by ultrafiltration, diafiltered against the final
formulation buffer for the target number of diavolumes, and further concentrated to the final
drug-substance target, with the transmembrane pressure and cross-flow controlled through the
operation. The number of diavolumes, the transmembrane pressure and the final DS concentration
are the operating variables; membrane lot and buffer composition are controlled to platform
specifications and treated as identity/quality-controlled inputs rather than characterized
variables [@amab2009].

## Analytical methods

Product concentration and the product-quality attributes were measured by validated methods
(@tbl-methods). The DS concentration was determined by protein A₂₈₀ (**AMV-3019**); size
variants (aggregate/HMW) by SEC-HPLC (**AMV-3011**) and charge variants by icIEF
(**AMV-3013**) to confirm the attributes are unchanged across the operation. Method
performance characteristics are summarized in Appendix B.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(sop_table(sops=[], amvs=UFDF_AMV_REFS))
```

: Validated analytical methods used in the evaluation. {#tbl-methods}

## Sampling plan

Each run was sampled at the final drug-substance pool for concentration and for the size- and
charge-variant attributes, and the product mass across the operation was recorded for the
step-yield calculation; the diafiltration exchange was monitored to confirm buffer-exchange
completeness. Runs at the parameter set-points were replicated to quantify the reproducibility
of yield and final concentration.

## Statistical methods

Because no drug-substance product-quality CQA is affected, the operation was evaluated
univariately rather than by a designed experiment. Each parameter was varied one factor at a
time across its characterization range, holding the others at their set-points, and the
process-performance measures — step yield, buffer-exchange completeness and final DS
concentration — were summarized against the parameter level. Reproducibility of yield and
final concentration was estimated from the replicated set-point runs. Parameter ranges were
judged acceptable where the performance measures remained within their platform targets and
the product-quality CQAs were unchanged.

## Parameters, ranges and the knowledge space

`{python} n_params` parameters were evaluated (@tbl-param). The characterization range of each
parameter ("PAR" column) defines the edges of the explored knowledge space and the basis of
the proven acceptable range; the NOR is the tighter range at which the parameter is controlled
routinely. Classification is an output of the evaluation (§8).

```{python}
show(report_params(UO))
```

: UF/DF process parameters, set-points, ranges and post-characterization classification. {#tbl-param}

## Univariate ranging

Each parameter was evaluated one factor at a time across its characterization range; none was
carried into a multivariate design because prior knowledge and the Pre-Characterization Risk
Assessment indicated no credible drug-substance CQA impact. The product-quality CQAs were
confirmed unchanged across the ranging.

# Results

## Process performance and reproducibility

At the nominal (set-point) condition the operation recovered antibody with a UF/DF step yield
of `{python} pct(ufdf_yield)` (`{python} f"{mass_in:,}"` g product mass in,
`{python} f"{mass_out:,}"` g out), completing the purification train at an overall process
yield of `{python} pct(cum_after)` and delivering `{python} f"{ds_mass_kg:.1f}"` kg of drug
substance at the target concentration of `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L. The set-point
replicates confirmed that step yield and final concentration are reproducible, establishing
that the operation delivers drug substance of consistent concentration and buffer composition.

## Univariate ranging of the operating parameters

Across the characterization range of each parameter, the process-performance measures remained
within their platform targets and the product-quality CQAs were unchanged:

- **Number of diavolumes.** Increasing the number of diavolumes improves the completeness of
  the buffer exchange (lowering residual old-buffer components) at the cost of longer process
  time; buffer-exchange completeness and yield remained acceptable across the range, and the
  NOR was confirmed as the window that assures complete exchange without unnecessary process
  time.
- **Transmembrane pressure.** Increasing the transmembrane pressure raises the permeate flux
  and shortens process time but, above the range, risks membrane fouling and concentration
  polarization; flux and yield remained within target across the range, and the NOR was
  confirmed as the window that balances throughput against fouling.
- **Final DS concentration.** As the controlled output attribute of the operation, the final
  DS concentration was delivered on target across the operating conditions, confirming a
  consistent drug-substance concentration.

## No product-quality impact

The size-variant (aggregate) and charge-variant results confirmed that these attributes are
unchanged across the operation, and the glycan attributes — set in cell culture — are not
modified by concentration or buffer exchange. The evaluation therefore confirms that UF/DF has
no drug-substance product-quality impact, consistent with the A-Mab case study, in which the
operation is a formulation / mass-balance step and the formulation characterization is reported
with the drug product [@amab2009].

# Process performance and consistency

Because the operation forms no drug-substance product-quality CQA, its robustness is expressed
as the consistency of its process-performance measures rather than as a multivariate design
space or a CQA capability index. The UF/DF yield of `{python} pct(ufdf_yield)` and the delivery
of drug substance at the `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L target, both reproducible at the
set-point and stable across the parameter ranges, establish that the operation reliably
delivers drug substance of consistent concentration and buffer composition at commercial scale.
The commercial-scale CQA capability is reported for the CQA-forming and CQA-clearing unit
operations in their respective reports and consolidated in **PCMR-001**; UF/DF contributes to it
only by preserving yield and delivering the drug substance on target.

# Parameter classification

Each parameter was classified on the A-Mab continuum from the demonstrated effects on process
performance and the absence of a drug-substance CQA impact (@tbl-class). The rationale is as
follows.

- **Number of diavolumes, transmembrane pressure, final DS concentration — KPP.** Each governs
  process performance — buffer-exchange completeness, permeate flux and process time, and the
  final concentration delivered — but none significantly impacts any drug-substance CQA; they
  are controlled for process performance and to deliver the drug substance on target.

No UF/DF parameter is a CPP, because the operation forms no drug-substance product-quality
attribute; formulation-related criticality, where applicable, is assessed under the
drug-product program.

```{python}
#| output: asis
d = report_params(UO)[["Parameter", "Class", "Study"]]
show(d)
```

: Post-characterization parameter classification. {#tbl-class}

# Contribution to the control strategy

UF/DF is not a control point for any drug-substance product-quality CQA; its contribution to
the overall control strategy is to complete the purification train at consistent yield and to
deliver the drug substance at its target concentration and buffer composition. That
contribution comprises: control of the number of diavolumes, the transmembrane pressure and the
final DS concentration to their NORs for reproducible buffer exchange, throughput and
concentration; in-process monitoring of the final concentration and buffer-exchange
completeness; and membrane life-cycle control. The drug-substance product-quality CQAs are set
and cleared upstream (reported in the paired unit-operation reports and consolidated in
**PCMR-001**), and the formulation control strategy is established under the drug-product
program.

# Discussion

The evaluation confirms the expected role of UF/DF: a formulation / mass-balance operation that
concentrates and buffer-exchanges the pool to the drug-substance target without forming or
modifying any drug-substance product-quality attribute. The operating parameters influence
buffer-exchange completeness, throughput and the final concentration in the directions
established by platform knowledge, and their ranges are justified on process-performance
grounds. The principal limitation is inherent to scale-down evaluation: absolute yield, flux and
buffer-exchange kinetics may shift modestly at commercial scale, which is why the model is
confirmed at scale during Stage 2 and the KPP ranges are carried forward with in-process
monitoring of the final concentration and buffer exchange. The evaluation did not identify any
parameter requiring critical (CPP) control within the studied ranges; formulation
characterization is addressed under the drug-product program.

# Conclusions

The A-Mab UF/DF operation is well understood and robust as a formulation / mass-balance step.
It sets or modifies no drug-substance product-quality CQA; it recovers antibody at a step yield
of `{python} pct(ufdf_yield)`, completes the process at an overall yield of
`{python} pct(cum_after)`, and delivers `{python} f"{ds_mass_kg:.1f}"` kg of drug substance at
the `{python} f"{ds_conc:g}"` g/L target; and its parameters are classified KPP with a
data-supported rationale. The parameter ranges and classifications provide the basis for the
Stage 2 operating ranges and the process-performance elements of the drug-substance control
strategy; the formulation characterization is reported with the drug product. This report rolls
up into the Process Characterization Master Report (**PCMR-001**) and provides the parameter
risk basis for the post-characterization process risk assessment.

# Deviations from the plan {.unnumbered}

No deviations from **PCP-010** were recorded. All planned ranging runs were executed and all
planned measures were recorded on the qualified scale-down UF/DF model.
